outcomes.name: vendored engines are byte-identical copies of app/ and the sw stamp is current (build --check)
--check notices a drifted vendor copy and a stale precache stamp; writing repairs them
service worker precaches every file of the app and nothing else (AC-2)
manifest is installable: name, scope, standalone, 192 and 512 PNG icons that exist and have those sizes
page contract: strict CSP, no inline script or style, no remote assets, no unsafe sinks
every relative import in mobile/ resolves to a shipped file, and the engines come from vendor/
the Pages workflow can only be started by hand and never deploys by default (hosting is undecided)
five screens, a photosensitivity confirmation before the strobe, and a persistent SPL banner
the phone and the desktop run the same format code
export round-trip from a real speed measurement: desktop parse, matching hash, same numbers (AC-5, AC-6)
export hash tamper is detected by the desktop parser
user agent can be redacted and never reaches the export
QR: a normal result is one QR; a large one is several, and each renders as a data-URI image
file name carries the kind, a compact UTC stamp and the .deckchek-mobile.json extension
an export that holds a value the format refuses throws instead of writing a bad file
Mobile edited export details reach text, file, share and clipboard with the same current checksum
Mobile explicit blanks omit saved hints and editing retires the visible QR until it is regenerated
Mobile blank visible export fields are authoritative and change-only edits also refresh the panel
Mobile current export details and redaction survive denied preference writes over readable old settings
Mobile recognizes all five declared routes and supported prefixes
Mobile falls back to Speed for empty, unsupported and inherited names
Mobile preserves result IDs and existing first-segment routing
export round-trip: parse returns the same measurements and a matching hash
hash is stable under key order and fractional numbers are hashed as decimal strings
tampering changes the hash: a warning, not a block
validator rejects unknown versions, wrong format, NaN/Infinity and oversize input
parse drops unknown fields and never returns the input objects
small exports are one plain-JSON QR; large ones split into frames that reassemble in any order
frame errors are specific: missing frame, mixed exports, damaged frame
QR framing preserves significant spaces at both sides of a frame boundary
desktop import preserves a significant-space-ended frame pasted last
QR options are bounded before even a single plain-JSON result is returned
framing preserves code points and refuses counts that the v1 headers cannot represent
framed wire accounting includes CRLF and a final line ending without raising the 1 MB cap
framed output must stay one frame per line while small plain JSON remains unchanged
direct frame joining keeps result-style type errors and the complete raw input budget
a production export populated to its field limits remains inside the default QR budget
history run: origin phone, tagged measurements, asset link, device label, no calibration
buildExport applies limits and drops unknown fields
structure: finders, separators, timing, dark module, format info
round trip: ASCII, URL, JSON, UTF-8, ECC L and M, versions 1-10
every byte length 0..200 round-trips at both levels (versions 1-10)
level M is never smaller than L, and capacity is enforced
qrSvg: valid-looking svg, quiet zone, escaped label, deterministic
the decoder is not vacuous: a flipped data module breaks Reed-Solomon or the text

limits: The six-file focused gate is not a complete-source gate.
Actual screen modules ran through a DOM fixture; file, share and clipboard boundaries were in-memory doubles.
The smoke module was syntax-parsed only; no browser or native behavior was exercised.
The predecessor complete gate remains held; issue #72 remains unresolved.
No numerical repair, diagnosis, full-suite rerun or qualification bypass is established.
